title-group.article-title: Analytical validation of a multiplex digital PCR assay for ESR1 alterations.

contrib-group.aff: Synthetic Oncology Research Center, Test City

permissions.copyright-statement: Synthetic test data generated for TNQTech evaluation; not a real publication.

abstract.p: Background: Accurate detection of ESR1 alterations is important for treatment selection in hormone receptor-positive metastatic breast cancer. We developed a rapid multiplex digital PCR assay intended for use with limited clinical specimens. Methods: The assay was evaluated using reference standards and archived clinical samples with predefined alteration status. Analytical sensitivity, analytical specificity, precision, and reproducibility were assessed across three reagent lots and two operators. Results were compared with an orthogonal sequencing method. Results: The study included 196 specimens. Positive agreement was 97.4% and negative agreement was 98.8%. The limit of detection was 0.25% variant allele fraction. No clinically meaningful difference was observed across reagent lots or operators, and repeatability exceeded 95%. Conclusions: The multiplex digital PCR assay demonstrated high analytical performance for detection of ESR1 alterations using limited specimen input. Clinical validation is warranted before routine implementation in hormone receptor-positive metastatic breast cancer. Research Sponsor: None.
